related_questions.question: How do I get my DUI expunged off my records in California?
related_questions.snippet: You will file a petition for expungement with the court that handled your DUI case. This requires completing the appropriate forms, including a "Petition for Dismissal" under Penal Code Section 1203.4, and paying a filing fee, which varies by county. If you cannot afford the fee, you may apply for a fee waiver.

related_questions.question: What is the difference between 1203.4 and 1203.4 a?
related_questions.snippet: Generally, 1203.4 is for people who obtained a probationary sentence for a felony or a misdemeanor. By contrast, 1203.4a is for people who did not serve any probation for a misdemeanor or an infraction.

related_questions.question: How much does it cost to expunge a DUI in California?

text_blocks.snippet: In California, the cost to expunge a DUI (Driving Under the Influence) conviction typically ranges from $500 to $4,000, depending on the complexity of the case and whether legal representation is used.

list.snippet: Most California counties charge a fee for filing the expungement petition, generally ranging from $125 to $175, according to Rubin Law Office.
These fees are set by the individual courts and are non-refundable.
Some courts may offer fee waivers for those who qualify based on financial hardship.
Legal representation is not mandatory, but many individuals choose to hire an attorney for guidance and to increase their chances of success.
Attorney fees can vary significantly based on the attorney's experience, the complexity of the case, and the attorney's location.
Fees can range from a few hundred dollars to $1,000 or more, according to Simmrin Law Group.
Some attorneys offer flat fees, while others charge hourly rates.
You may incur additional costs for things like certified copies of documents, notarization, or potential court reporter services.
Parking fees for court appearances and obtaining records from various agencies could also add to the expense.

list.title: Complexity of the case:
list.snippet: Cases involving multiple DUI offenses, probation violations, or complications related to Proposition 47 will likely be more expensive.

list.title: Attorney's experience:
list.snippet: Attorneys with more experience in handling DUI expungements may charge higher fees.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: Fees can vary based on the area where the attorney practices.

list.title: Whether you choose to represent yourself:
list.snippet: If you choose to handle the expungement process yourself, you will only incur court filing fees and any other additional costs.
